QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_28

question.text: Under the 2025 SEBI (AIF) amendment allowing Cat I and II AIFs to offer co-investment via a CIV scheme, which statement is TRUE?

answer.text: A separate CIV scheme must be launched for EACH co-investment and can invest in only ONE investee company
Angel Funds are allowed to launch CIV schemes
A single CIV scheme can invest in MULTIPLE investee companies
CIV schemes can invest in units of other AIFs

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI (AIF) (Second Amendment) Regulations 2025 (w.e.f. Sep 9, 2025): a SEPARATE CIV scheme per co-investment, each investing in ONLY ONE investee company. Angel Funds are explicitly EXCLUDED. CIV schemes CANNOT invest in units of AIFs. The Trap: Each of the other three options directly violates the 2025 amendment. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests this 2025 amendment. It is a fresh regulatory item specifically for Cat I/II, so XIX-D will stress it. Manager's Pro-Tip: CIV-scheme route avoids the dual PMS + AIF registration pain. Plan to file a 'shelf placement memorandum' via a merchant banker — one shelf PM can cover multiple CIV schemes as long as each is for a single investee.
